catalog.title: OptVec train
catalog.mac: Research methods: Author request, review inputs, then open execution and evidence. Both CLIs use science interview/draft/publish and the same managed engine.
outputs: Operation report and its provenance; inspect the declared run/config output.
catalog.restriction: Explicit config, reviewed input hashes and a fresh engine plan are required. GPU work requires immutable model revisions. Outputs are new records; local/Slurm execution uses the existing scientific owner. Native MLX numerical equivalence is not claimed. Remote training and analysis outputs are retained; the diagnostic cleanup policy does not authorize their removal.

interview.title: Train a steering vector
interview.purpose: Teach a vector to favor a chosen answer over an alternative, while preserving other judgments and abilities. Start with your own choice prompts or prompts prepared from study outputs.

fields.label: Model to execute
fields.help: Choose the prepared model; this does not acquire weights.

fields.label: Model commit
fields.help: The exact version of the model. Inspect the selected model to fill its commit automatically; an agent can also supply a verified commit. This prevents silently switching model versions.

fields.label: Injection layer
fields.help: The transformer layer where the learned vector is added (zero-based). Choose a layer supported by your model and study design; no universal best layer is assumed.

fields.label: Dose in residual-norm units
fields.help: Steering strength relative to the model’s typical activation size. For example, 0.1 means one tenth of the measured residual norm. This is not a J-space artifact-norm multiple.

fields.label: Artifact supplying the residual norm
fields.help: Choose an inspected artifact with a residual norm table, or explicitly provide alphaAbsolute under advanced settings.

fields.label: Target training items
fields.help: Examples of the behavior to change. For each prompt, state two answer choices and the answer to encourage. Training increases its log-probability relative to the other choice. Study outputs must first be authored into this choice-row format; they are not consumed directly. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Selection / validation items
fields.help: Separate examples of the same behavior, used for checkpoint selection or monitoring. Do not reuse training or final-test rows. A declared fixed-step run can omit this file. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Behaviors to preserve
fields.help: Judgments you want to leave unchanged. The optimizer penalizes changes to the unsteered model’s answer probabilities on these prompts, rather than teaching the target label as a new answer. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Anchor validation items
fields.help: Separate preservation examples for checking whether the trained vector changes judgments you meant to preserve. Keep them distinct from the preservation training rows. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Capability training controls
fields.help: Questions with objectively correct answers, such as basic reasoning or factual tasks. Here target is the correct answer; the optimizer penalizes losing it. Use examples relevant to the abilities your study needs. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Maximum optimization steps
fields.help: Upper limit on optimizer updates, not the number of examples. The existing default is a starting setting to review, not a recommended value for every study.

fields.label: Name for this reading
fields.help: A new immutable result will be created.

interview.claimBoundary: Training objective improvement is not held-out behavioral validation.
questions: What behavior should change, and in which direction?
Which judgments and capabilities must remain stable?
Is checkpoint selection based on validation, or are fixed steps predeclared? Keep final test data separate.
